title: ACT ON THE PERFORMANCE OF DUTIES BY MILITARY POLICE
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to ensure the lawful execution of duties and prevent human rights violations that may occur in the course of performing duties by prescribing matters necessary for the performance of duties by military police.

Article 2 (Basic principles for performance of duties) (1) The authority of military police prescribed in this Act shall be exercised to the minimum extent necessary for the performance of duties and shall not be abused.
  (2) Military police shall not collect or use information beyond the scope of legitimate duties prescribed by this Act.

Article 3 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Dec. 13, 2022>
  1. "Military police" means officers, warrant officers, noncommissioned officers, and enlisted members in the branch under Article 43(1) of the Military Court Act, and civilian personnel in the military service under the Act on the Personnel Management of Civilian Military Employee, who belong to military police units and perform police duties relating to military affairs, as prescribed by Presidential Decree;
  2. “Military area” means military bases and military installations under subparagraphs 1 and 2 of Article 2 of the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act, and areas north of the Civilian Control Line under Article 5(1)1a of that Act;
  3. “Military police equipment” means devices and instruments necessary for the performance of duties by military police, including weapons, military police gear, tear gas agents and launchers therefor, breath analyzers, speed measuring devices, forensic instruments, coastal surveillance instruments, communication devices, and devices and instruments for vehicles, vessels, and aircraft;
  4. “Hazardous military police equipment” means military police equipment that may cause harm to the life or body of another person;
  5. “Military police gear” means devices and instruments prescribed by Presidential Decree, including handcuffs, restraint ropes, police batons, stun guns, conducted energy weapons, and shields, which military police carry and use in performing duties such as arresting offenders and suppressing crimes;
  6. “Sprayers, etc.” means sprayers under the Act on the Safety Management of Guns, Swords, and Explosives, tear-producing agents such as tear gas used therefor, and tear gas bombs;
  7. “Weapons” means pistols, rifles, swords, and other instruments manufactured to inflict harm on the life or body of a person.

Article 4 (Persons subject to application) (1) Duties of military police under this Act shall, in principle, apply to military service members and civilian personnel in the military service subject to the Military Personnel Management Act and the Act on the Personnel Management of Civilian Military Employee.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), Articles 7 and 8 shall also apply to civilians (including foreigners) residing in or temporarily visiting military areas.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), Articles 11 through 14 shall also apply to Koreans and foreigners who commit crimes falling under Article 1(4) of the Military Criminal Act.

Article 5 (Scope of duties of military police and command and supervision thereof) (1) Military police shall perform the following duties under the command and supervision of the commander of the unit in which a military police unit is established: <Amended on Dec. 13, 2022>
  1. Protection and security of, and counterterrorism responses for, major military personnel and facilities;
  2. Maintenance of military traffic, operation, and navigation order and prevention of hazards;
  3. Collection of information on, prevention, suppression, and investigation of crimes prescribed in subparagraph 1 of Article 44 of the Military Court Act;
  4. Management of persons in military custody under the Act on the Execution of Criminal Penalties in the Armed Forces and the Treatment of Military Inmates;
  5. Protection of victims of military crimes;
  6. Mutual cooperation with the police, prosecutors’ offices, and other investigative agencies;
  7. International cooperation with the United States Forces Korea and foreign military police;
  8. Other activities for the establishment of military discipline and maintenance of order.
  (2) The Minister of National Defense shall establish an Investigation Headquarters under the Ministry of National Defense to comprehensively oversee policies concerning military police as the highest commander and supervisor of military police duties.
  (3) The Chiefs of Staff of each service shall establish a Military Police Office or Military Police Corps to comprehensively oversee military police duties of units under their respective services as commanders and supervisors of military police duties for each service.
  (4) The commander of a unit in which a military police unit is established shall administer military police duties under his or her jurisdiction and command and supervise subordinate military police.
  (5) Enlisted members serving as military police shall assist in the performance of military police duties under the direction of supervisory personnel of the military police unit to which they belong (referring to officers, warrant officers, non-commissioned officers, and civilian personnel in the military service as prescribed in subparagraph 1 of Article 3).
  (6) Specific matters concerning the scope of duties of military police and command and supervision thereof shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Cooperation with Military Human Rights Protection Officer) Military police shall cooperate with matters requested by the Military Human Rights Protection Officer under Article 42 of the Framework Act on Military Status and Service (hereinafter referred to as the “Military Human Rights Protection Officer”) for the purpose of performing his or her duties, unless there are special circumstances.

Article 7 (Questioning in performance of duties and requests for accompaniment) (1) Military police may stop and question (hereafter referred to in this Article as “questioning in the performance of duties”) any person falling under any of the following subparagraphs within military areas, and in such cases may take measures necessary for identity verification, including presentation of an identification card:
  1. A person who, judging reasonably from suspicious behavior or other surrounding circumstances, is reasonably suspected of having committed or being about to commit any crime;
  2. A person deemed to have knowledge of a crime already committed or about to be committed.
  (2) Where military police deem that conducting questioning in the performance of duties at the place where a person referred to in any subparagraph of paragraph (1) has been stopped would disadvantage such person or interfere with traffic, they may request that the person accompany them to a nearby military police unit, checkpoint, etc. (hereafter referred to in this Article as “military police unit, etc.”) for questioning. In such cases, the person requested to accompany military police may refuse such request; provided, a person not prescribed in Article 4(1) may be requested to accompany military police to a nearby police station, district unit, precinct, or branch office (including local maritime police agencies; hereafter referred to in this Article as “police agency”) unless it is clearly recognized that such person has committed a crime falling under Article 1(4) of the Military Criminal Act.
  (3) Military police may, when conducting questioning in the performance of duties, investigate whether a person possesses a weapon or deadly weapon.
  (4) When conducting questioning in the performance of duties or requesting accompaniment, military police shall present identification verifying their status, disclose their affiliation and names, and explain the purpose and reasons for the questioning or accompaniment, and where accompaniment is requested, shall also specify the place of accompaniment.
  (5) Military police shall directly notify the commander of the unit to which the person accompanying them pursuant to paragraph (2) belongs, and the person’s family members, relatives, or other persons concerned, of the identity of the accompanying military police, the place of accompaniment, and the purpose and grounds for the accompaniment, or shall provide the person with an opportunity to immediately contact family members, relatives, or other persons concerned, and shall inform the person that he or she has the right to the assistance of counsel.
  (6) Military police shall not detain an accompanied person at a military police unit, etc. or police agency for more than 6 hours, and where the person so requests, accompaniment shall immediately be terminated.
  (7) A person questioned or requested to accompany military police pursuant to paragraphs (1) through (3) shall not be detained except in accordance with statutes governing procedures for litigation in military courts, and shall not be compelled to answer against his or her will.

Article 8 (Prevention and suppression of crimes) Where military police deem that a criminal act is about to be committed in their presence within a military area, they may issue necessary warnings to the relevant persons in order to prevent such act, and may suppress such act in urgent cases where the act is likely to cause harm to the life or body of a person or serious damage to property.

Article 9 (Entry for prevention of danger) (1) Where military police deem it unavoidable in order to prevent harm to life, body, or property or rescue victims where a dangerous situation occurs within a military area, they may, upon reasonable judgment of the circumstances, enter another person’s land, building, vessel, or vehicle to the extent necessary.
  (2) Where military police enter pursuant to paragraph (1), they shall present identification verifying their status and shall not unreasonably interfere with the legitimate business of the relevant persons.

Article 10 (Maintenance of order in traffic, flight, and navigation order) (1) Military police shall prevent and remove dangers and obstacles to traffic, operation, and navigation in order to maintain safe and smooth traffic, operation, and navigation order within military areas, and may crack down on acts prohibited under Articles 44 and 45 of the Road Traffic Act, Articles 39 and 40 of the Sea Traffic Safety Act, and Article 57 of the Aviation Safety Act. <Amended on Jul. 25, 2023>
  (2) When conducting crackdowns under paragraph (1), military police may determine whether a person is intoxicated through a breath test. In such cases, the person subject to the crackdown shall comply with the request for measurement by military police.
  (3) A person who objects to the results of measurement under paragraph (2) may, upon his or her consent, be reexamined by means of blood sampling or other methods.
  (4) Specific matters concerning the performance of duties under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Use of military police equipment) (1) Military police may use military police equipment in the performance of duties; provided, hazardous military police equipment shall be used only after necessary safety education and safety inspections have been completed.
  (2) Military police shall not arbitrarily modify military police equipment or attach arbitrary equipment thereto and use such equipment in a manner different from ordinary methods of use, thereby causing harm to the life or body of another person.
  (3) Hazardous military police equipment shall be used to the minimum extent necessary.
  (4) Where the Minister of National Defense intends to newly introduce hazardous military police equipment, he or she shall conduct a safety inspection in accordance with Presidential Decree and submit a report on the results thereof to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly. In such cases, external experts shall participate in the safety inspection.
  (5) Types of hazardous military police equipment, standards for use thereof, and standards for safety education and safety inspections shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Use of military police gear) Military police may, upon reasonable judgment of the circumstances, use military police gear where there are reasonable grounds to deem it necessary for performing the duties prescribed in the following subparagraphs:
  1. Arrest of a person caught in the act of committing a crime or a person who has committed a crime punishable by death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment with or without labor for a maximum term of not less than 3 years, or prevention of the escape thereof;
  2. Defense and protection of the life or body of themselves or other persons;
  3. Suppression of resistance to the performance of official duties.

Article 13 (Use of sprayers, etc.) Where unavoidable for performing any of the following duties, military police may, upon the judgment of the officer in charge at the scene, use sprayers, etc. within the minimum extent necessary:
  1. Arrest of an offender or prevention of the escape thereof;
  2. Suppression of the occurrence of imminent harm to the life, body, or property of themselves or other persons, or to military areas.

Article 14 (Use of weapons) (1) Where military police have reasonable grounds to deem it necessary for the arrest of an offender, prevention of escape, defense and protection of their own or another person’s life or body, or suppression of resistance against the performance of official duties, they may, upon reasonable judgment of the circumstances, use weapons to the minimum extent necessary; provided, they shall not inflict harm on any person except in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the act constitutes self-defense or necessity under Articles 21 and 22 of the Criminal Act;
  2. Where there are reasonable grounds to deem that there is no other means, except through the use of weapons, to prevent the relevant act or arrest the relevant offender in any of the following cases:
  a. Where a person who has committed, or is reasonably suspected of having committed, a crime punishable by death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment with or without labor for a maximum term of not less than 3 years resists, or attempts to escape, the execution of duties by military police;
  b. Where a person resists, or attempts to escape, the execution of duties by military police in the course of executing a warrant of arrest or detention, or a warrant of seizure or search;
  c. Where a third person resists military police in an attempt to help a person falling under item a or b escape;
  d. Where an offender or a person who has caused a disturbance continues to resist while carrying weapons, dangerous instruments, or other dangerous objects and refuses to comply after having received at least 3 orders from military police to discard such objects or surrender.
  (2) When using weapons, military police shall ensure that no damage is inflicted on persons unrelated to the cause giving rise to the use of weapons, and where the use of weapons is no longer necessary in light of the surrounding circumstances, they shall immediately discontinue such use.
  (3) Where military police use weapons pursuant to paragraph (1), they shall report the grounds and circumstances thereof to the commander of the military police unit to which they belong without delay, and the commander of the relevant military police unit shall, in turn, report them to the commander of the superior unit without delay.

Article 15 (Safety education on military police equipment) (1) The commander of a military police unit shall provide education on the methods of use, management, safety, and other matters related to military police equipment.
  (2) The commander of a military police unit shall conduct regular safety inspections on hazardous military police equipment.
  (3) The commander of a military police unit shall neither have a person who has not received the safety education under paragraph (1) perform the duties of military police nor allow the use of hazardous military police equipment that has not undergone the safety inspection under paragraph (2).
  (4) Specific matters concerning the methods of education on the use, management, safety, and other matters related to military police equipment under paragraph (1), and the standards for safety inspections under paragraph (2), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Retention of records of use) Where an electronic shock device, electronic shock gun, sprayer, etc., or weapon is used, the commander of the military police unit to which the user belongs shall record and retain the date and time, place, subject, person responsible for the scene, type, quantity, and other relevant matters concerning such use.

Article 17 Deleted. <Jan. 7, 2025>

Article 18 (Guidance and supervision for human rights protection) The commander of a military police unit shall have the responsibility to provide guidance and supervision to ensure that military police under his or her command do not infringe human rights in the course of performing their duties, and where the commander becomes aware of facts related to a human rights violation, he or she shall notify the Military Human Rights Protection Officer or the military legal officer in charge of human rights under Article 59-2 of the Military Personnel Management Act and shall take appropriate measures.

Article 19 (Penalty provisions) (1) Military police who violate duties prescribed for military police under this Act or abuse their authority, thereby causing harm to another person, shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won.
  (2) Any person who, having reasonable grounds to be recognized as being under the influence of alcohol, fails to comply with a request for measurement by military police under Article 10(2) shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not less than 1 year and not more than 5 years, or by a fine of not less than 5 million won and not more than 20 million won.
  (3) Any navigator who operates or directs the operation of the helm of a vessel under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Ship Personnel Act (including a foreign vessel falling under any of the items of that subparagraph), any pilot who conducts pilotage, or any aviation personnel who operates an aircraft under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Aviation Safety Act, in violation of Article 10(2) by failing to comply with a request for measurement by military police, shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

ADDENDA <Act No. 17680, Dec. 22, 2020>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force 6 months after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Transitional measures concerning existing organizations and business affairs under their jurisdiction)
The business affairs of units performing the duties prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 5(1) pursuant to previous statutes or regulations as at the time this Act enters into force shall be succeeded to by military police units, and military personnel and civilian personnel in the military service belonging to such units shall be deemed military police.
Article 3 (Transitional measures concerning acts of performing duties)
Investigative activities, guard duties, security duties, management of persons in military custody, and other acts of performing duties carried out by military personnel and civilian personnel in the military service belonging to units performing the duties prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 5(1) pursuant to previous statutes or regulations as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed acts performed by military police under this Act.
